rationale: Re-derived at 3018a659, lens contract stability. All three of my round-2 asks are delivered, and I verified each live rather than taking the commit message's word. G-r2-1 CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION — and I judge the divergence genuinely eliminated, not relocated: the recording class now consumes recording.EventsPath/ManifestPath's OWN resolved answers, called with the same root argument the claim's step 7.5 write itself uses, so the guard's predicted target and the actual write target are the same function evaluated on the same inputs — whatever tree workspace.SpecDir picks, both see it, and no second parallel resolution exists to drift. The gate is pure containment of that resolved target in cwd's canonical toplevel. I ran the mandated custom-worktree_root fixture (TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_EnumerationPin_CustomWorktreeRootRecording, PASS 42s): it reproduces my round-2 decoy exactly — custom root configured, recording enabled, manifest seeded at repoRoot where SpecDir's non-cfg-aware probe actually resolves, a genuine decoy spec worktree present at the custom root, claim invoked from repoRoot — and its len(want)==2 fixture-sanity assertion is a true red-on-revert pin (the round-2 samePath gate predicts 0 there and fails the test before the claim even runs). G-r2-2 CLOSED: toplevelOf routes through git rev-parse --show-toplevel + EvalSymlinks, containedRel emits toplevel-relative slash paths matching porcelain's own convention, and both the subdirectory-invocation and symlink-alias-invocation refusal e2e tests pass through the real binary (54s/52s, byte-identical no-op asserted). The resolveContainingDirs leaf-name subtlety (resolve ancestor dirs, never the leaf, because porcelain reports a symlinked .gitignore under its own tracked name) is correct and was itself caught by the bead's own e2e fixture — evidence the fixtures bite. G-r2-3 CLOSED: the stale first-draft doc block is gone; the rewritten header states the one containment mechanism, names the SpecDir non-cfg-aware divergence explicitly as the reason for trusting recording's own resolution, and the ADR-0025 amendment now describes the shipped mechanism (containment as the single source of truth, both conditional classes, real-claim fixtures as the anti-drift pin) instead of the falsified 'exactly (a)(b)(c) EMPTY' story. I also traced the remaining seams for a relocated divergence and found only fail-closed or inert residuals, none fail-open (see findings). Unit suites for internal/next and internal/gitutil pass. Bead worktree left byte-identical (git status clean).

findings.title: Custom-worktree_root divergence eliminated by construction, verified live
findings.detail: The by-construction argument holds: ComputeEntangleablePaths calls recording.EventsPath/ManifestPath(repoRoot, specID) — the identical calls next.go step 7.5 makes — and gates on containedRel(toplevelOf(cwd), resolvedTarget). There is no replicated resolution left for the recording class to drift against. The one theoretical check-vs-use window (SpecDir's answer flipping between guard and step 7.5 if a spec worktree's spec dir materializes mid-claim) can only move the write into a tree that did not exist at guard time — where pre-existing dirt is impossible — so its worst case is a stale armed path that over-blocks, never a waved-through entanglement. Fixture run by this reviewer: PASS, with the pre-claim prediction (2 recording paths at repoRoot, despite the cfg-aware anchor pointing at the decoy custom worktree) exactly matching the real claim's porcelain diff.

findings.title: Canonical-toplevel containment closes the subdirectory and symlink-alias gaps
findings.detail: toplevelOf(cwd) + containedRel produce toplevel-relative paths matching porcelain's base convention (which I verified empirically in round 2), with EvalSymlinks canonicalization on both sides so a symlink alias of the tree and the tree itself share one identity. Both mandated real-claim refusal regressions pass through the actual binary with byte-identical no-op proof. The non-git-dir degrade (toplevelOf falling back to cwd, still symlink-resolved to avoid /var-vs-/private/var spurious escapes on macOS) is a sound ambient-helper fallback and unreachable on the production path, where FindRoot has already succeeded.

findings.title: Derivation comments and ADR-0025 amendment now tell the one true story
findings.detail: The first draft's 'ALWAYS under repoRoot / repoRoot == cwd' text is gone. The rewritten ComputeEntangleablePaths header describes containment as the single mechanism and explicitly documents WHY the recording class trusts SpecDir's own resolution (its worktree probe hardcodes .worktrees, so replicating it would duplicate-drift). The ADR-0025 amendment replaces the falsified empty-enumeration derivation with the two-conditional-class containment rule and names the real e2e fixtures — recording-enabled, gitignore-absent, custom-worktree_root — as the anti-drift pin.

findings.title: Accepted residuals, all fail-closed or inert — recorded for the tally, no change required
findings.detail: (1) claimAnchorRoot still replicates MindspecExecutor.resolveAnchorRoot for the .gitignore class with no compile-time coupling; the replication is currently line-for-line faithful (verified round 2) and any future drift shows red in the real-claim e2e pins, which diff-match a genuine DispatchBead run. (2) containedRel is filesystem containment, not git-tree membership: a resolved target inside a NESTED linked worktree under the toplevel (e.g. the spec worktree's recording copy while invoking from the main checkout) can be armed as an entry that either never matches porcelain (the nested root is gitignored — inert) or over-blocks via the collapsed-untracked-dir ancestor rule (the nested root is not ignored — fail-closed, and defensible: the claim would write into a region the observed tree reports as dirt). (3) Dirt residing in a DIFFERENT checkout than the invoking one (e.g. a dirty manifest inside the spec worktree while claiming from the main checkout) remains invisible to this guard by the round-1 observability doctrine; the pre-128 all-dirt block had exactly the same single-tree scope, so this is no regression. (4) workspace.SpecDir's nil-cfg worktree probe remains a PRE-EXISTING defect outside this bead's scope — under a custom worktree_root it sends recording WRITES to repoRoot instead of the spec worktree for every recording call site, not just this guard; the guard is now correct regardless, but a follow-up bd bead for SpecDir cfg-awareness is worth filing if one does not already exist.
